cohort: The study included 75 children aged 5-9 years, divided into three groups: children born prematurely, children delivered by caesarean section, and children born on time by natural means.
finding: The study found a significantly higher risk of Sensory Processing Disorder (SPD) in prematurely born children (84%) and children delivered by C-section (80%) compared to those born on time by vaginal birth.
mod_finding: Children delivered by C-section were found to be at a statistically significant higher risk (80%) of Sensory Processing Disorder compared to those born on time by vaginal birth.
